meta_title: Services | Margarita Makri, Psychologist in Larissa
meta_description: Adult psychotherapy, couples therapy, adolescents, anxiety and panic attacks, depression and eating disorders, in Larissa, Greece and online.
title: Services
lead: Every therapy starts with an initial assessment and is tailored to you. In-person sessions in Larissa and online.

items.title: Adult psychotherapy
items.summary: Individual sessions for anxiety, stress, depression and difficult stages of life.
items.lead: A safe and confidential space where we look together at what troubles you and work on it in practical ways.
items.for_you_title: It may concern you if you
items.for_you:
- feel intense anxiety or stress
- have low mood or have lost interest in things
- are going through a major change or life crisis
- want to change patterns that keep repeating
items.how:
- initial assessment and shared goals
- structured sessions with practical exercises
- regular review of progress
items.note: Pace and duration are tailored to you. No specific outcome is guaranteed, but there is a clear plan and real collaboration.

items.title: Couples therapy
items.summary: Better communication and ways through the difficulties in your relationship.
items.lead: We work with both partners together, so you can understand the patterns that repeat and find new ways of communicating.
items.for_you_title: It may concern you if you
items.for_you:
- have frequent conflicts or feel distant
- are going through a transition, such as parenthood or a move
- want to strengthen your relationship
items.how:
- a joint meeting and agreed goals
- practising communication skills
- exercises between sessions
items.note: Therapy does not take sides and cannot guarantee a specific outcome for the relationship.

items.title: Adolescents
items.summary: Support for adolescents, adapted to their age, in collaboration with the family.
items.lead: Adolescents express themselves differently from adults. Sessions are adapted to their age, with parents involved where needed.
items.for_you_title: It may help if the adolescent
items.for_you:
- has anxiety, fears or low mood
- struggles at school or with friendships
- shows changes in behaviour or sleep

And if you, as parents, are looking for guidance.
items.how:
- keeping parents informed and working with them
- age-appropriate exercises
- respect for the adolescent's privacy, within ethical limits
items.note: Progress also depends on the family's consistency.

items.title: Anxiety and panic attacks
items.summary: Understanding and managing anxiety, panic and fears.
items.lead: Anxiety is a normal response, but when it becomes intense or persistent it affects everyday life. We learn how it works and how to manage it.
items.for_you_title: It may concern you if you
items.for_you:
- have panic attacks
- worry excessively or have social anxiety
- avoid situations because of fear
items.how:
- learning how anxiety works
- relaxation and thought-management techniques
- gradual exposure to situations you avoid
items.note: CBT has strong research support for anxiety, without guaranteeing the same result for everyone.

items.title: Depression
items.summary: Support through periods of low mood, fatigue and loss of interest.
items.lead: Depression affects mood, thinking and behaviour. We identify the cycles that keep it going and take small, achievable steps towards change.
items.for_you_title: It may concern you if you
items.for_you:
- feel persistent sadness or emptiness
- have lost motivation or energy
- have negative thoughts about yourself
items.how:
- gradually returning to enjoyable and meaningful activities
- examining negative thoughts
- working with a psychiatrist where needed
items.extra: Depression is defined as a set of reactions that show at a psychological, behavioural and biological level. It is seen as a person's reaction to a significant loss or a distressing event.
items.note: If you have thoughts of harming yourself, call [112](tel:112) or the Suicide Prevention Line [1018](tel:1018) immediately.

items.title: Eating disorders
items.summary: Support when your relationship with food, your body and your self-image becomes difficult.
items.lead: Eating disorders are not only about food, but also about how we think and feel about our body and ourselves. Together we understand what keeps the difficulty going and work step by step towards a more balanced relationship with food.
items.for_you_title: It may concern you if you
items.for_you:
- are strongly preoccupied with weight, body shape or calories
- follow strict diets or skip meals
- have episodes of binge eating and feel you lose control
- feel guilt or shame after eating
items.how:
- understanding the cycle that keeps the difficulty going
- gradually returning to a regular, balanced pattern of meals
- working on thoughts about body, weight and self-esteem
- working with a dietitian or doctor where needed
items.note: Eating disorders can also affect physical health, so in some cases medical follow-up is needed alongside therapy.

cta_text: At our first meeting we will clarify together what troubles you and which way of working suits you.
